thread_text:
incident-bot: PAGER: KV cache growth alert on prod cluster us-west-2. spike in cache size and tail latency for several shards. error rate up. paging jason_oncall :rotating_light:

jason_oncall: saw it. investigating now. p95 for generate-token spiked from 120ms -> 1.8s for some routes. error rate ~4.7% on replicas serving Llama-*-v2.

priya_sre: looking at eviction logs — eviction loop on several shards due to very large kv entries from repeated prefix-heavy prompts. continuous_batching aggregated massive prefixes into single cache keys.

sara_dev: confirmed heatmap: traffic concentrated to a handful of customers with long conversation prefixes + high streaming churn. continuous_batching window = 10s currently. that's letting very large composite requests create oversized KV entries.

marc_engineer: quick Q: do we have per-model batch_size_max? I think Llama v2 has none set in runtime defaults. that explains growth with MQA fallback when GQA model had new tokenization pattern.

priya_sre: mitigation plan: 1) flip continuous_batching.enabled=false globally for affected pool, 2) set kv.max_entry_size=2MB, 3) set per-model batch_size_max=64 for Llama and 96 for Qwen canary, 4) promote an immediate canary of the config and monitor 60s. happy to run commands if we agree.

jason_oncall: do it. prioritize minimizing customer errors. try per-pool toggle first so we can rollback quickly.

sara_dev: executing canary toggle on pool "inference-west-gpu-01" now. command:
```bash
# disable continuous batching for pool, canary on nodes 3,4
runtimectl update pool inference-west-gpu-01 --set continuous_batching.enabled=false --nodes 3,4
```

ops-bot: acknowledged command received. applying config change to nodes 3,4. will report back.

(30s later)

ops-bot: nodes 3,4 config applied. metrics streaming updated. ops-bot: after change p95 dropped from 1.8s -> 420ms on canary nodes. errors on canary -> 0.9%.

marc_engineer: good. we should propagate batch_size_max and kv.max_entry_size too. I'll push a config patch to the runtime group: patch id rtime-2026-05-01-01.

marc_engineer: patch command:
```yaml
runtime_patch: rtime-2026-05-01-01
settings:
  models:
    llama-v2*:
      batch_size_max: 64
    qwen-*:
      batch_size_max: 96
  kv:
    max_entry_bytes: 2097152
```

priya_sre: while rollout happens, increase eviction threshold so we don't thrash hot entries: `kv.eviction_threshold_percent=85` (was 65). we'll revert post-mitigation.

sara_dev: rolling patch to remaining nodes now in 3-minute wave to avoid sudden capacity drop. watch for mem pressure.

(3m later)

ops-bot: rollout progress: 30% -> 60% -> 90% -> 100%. no infra OOMs reported. p95 cluster-wide down to ~360ms. errors at 1.2% (from 4.7%).

jason_oncall: customer impact summary (initial): 12 tenants experienced degraded p95 and intermittent 5xxs. primary impacted models: llama-v2 variants under long-prefix sessions. approximate affected qps window ~ 09:02-09:22 UTC. no persistent data loss.

priya_sre: root cause hypothesis: continuous_batching combined long conversation prefixes into single cache entries. certain tokenization differences (GQA -> MQA fallback) produced very large keys; without per-model batch limits this caused KV growth and frequent evictions, triggering error cascades.

sara_dev: follow-ups: 1) add per-model default batch_size_max in model catalog, 2) add ingress request size limiter for prefix length > 64k tokens to reject or shard, 3) add better observability metric: `kv.entry_bytes_histogram` by model variant and customer id (for rate-limited retention).

marc_engineer: also propose adding a runtime flag to prefer model-variant fallback that avoids combining prefixes into a single cache key for MQA->GQA transitions. it's a small patch in key hashing.

jason_oncall: handoff: i'll keep monitoring for the next hour; handing on-call to priya_sre at 10:30 UTC. priya, full situational awareness: mitigations applied, cluster p95 stabilized ~350-420ms, errors down from 4.7% -> 1.2%. still watching for tail-case tenants.

priya_sre: taking handoff. i'll keep alerting thresholds tightened and notify CSMs for the 12 impacted tenants. drafting customer message template now.

sara_dev: customer message draft (internal):
"We observed elevated latency and transient errors affecting a subset of customers between 09:02-09:22 UTC. Cause: oversized KV cache entries triggered by a continuous-batching edge case with long conversation prefixes. We applied an emergency config to disable continuous batching for the affected pool and capped per-model batch sizes to limit KV entry growth. Latency and errors have reduced; we will follow up with permanent fixes and a timeline."

marc_engineer: logs/commands for postmortem capture:
```text
- runtimectl get pool inference-west-gpu-01 --history
- kubectl logs -l pool=inference-west-gpu-01 -n runtime | grep kv_eviction
- metrics query: sum(rate(kv_evictions_total[5m])) by (pool, model_variant)
```

ops-bot: alerting: existing pager rule eased; new temporary alert `kv_entry_size_high` created for 1h with threshold 1.6MB.

priya_sre: assigning action items:
- sara_dev: write customer-facing note and post to incidents-channel (ETA 30m).
- marc_engineer: implement per-model defaults in model catalog + key-hash patch (ETA 2d).
- jason_oncall: follow up on affected tenant list and flag priority accounts for 1:1 outreach (ETA 1h).
- ops-bot: keep temporary alert up for 1h and then auto-delete.

jason_oncall: final note before handoff: if we see a second spike after rollback of eviction_threshold, revert to canary-disable continuous_batching for pool immediately. leave pager quiet for non-critical alerts.

priya_sre: acknowledged. taking over now. handing note posted to /incident-handoff with summary and links to dashboards. :white_check_mark:
